chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥajjāl, from Thaʿlabah, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A man rises from the salat (prayer), then after he has finished he looks and sees that he had deviated from the qiblah to the right or the left. He said: His salat (prayer) has passed as valid, and what lies between the east and the west is qiblah.

key_terms.انْحَرَفَ: deviated or turned away from the intended direction
key_terms.مَضَتْ: has passed; here meaning it is accepted and need not be repeated

ai.seo_question: If someone realizes after salat (prayer) that he was slightly off the qiblah, does the prayer need to be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who discovers after completing salat (prayer) that he had turned somewhat away from the qiblah to the right or left. The Imam عليه السلام states that the prayer remains valid, indicating latitude in cases of slight directional deviation within the span between east and west.
